About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Join Anthropic's Commercial Legal team as a Technical AI implementation specialist, where you'll be responsible for leveraging Claude and other technologies to scale and increase efficiency of legal operations. You'll drive AI adoption across team workflows, optimize internal tooling, and lead cross-functional initiatives to enhance productivity. This role offers the unique opportunity to shape the future of legal operations through technology while working with Claude and other business critical systems.
Key responsibilities
Implement AI-powered solutions to streamline contract review and redlining processes
Manage integrations between existing legal systems and AI tools
Develop automated self-service solutions for high-volume, low-touch contracting processes, including FAQ chatbots and guided workflows
Create AI-based tools for handling commercial contract diligence requests
Optimize contract management platforms with AI capabilities
Create and manage comprehensive program plans, including timelines, budgets, and resource allocation, to guide project execution
Build and maintain metrics dashboards to track efficiency improvements
Establish practical governance processes for AI use in legal operations
Coordinate with Engineering and Product teams on solution development
Identify and mitigate potential risks and issues that could affect program success, ensuring proactive problem-solving
Minimum qualifications
Experience evaluating and implementing legal technology platforms such as contract management systems, workflow management systems, or document management tools
Show genuine curiosity about AI/ML applications and hands-on experience with LLM tools (especially Claude!)
Possess excellent problem-solving skills and can translate legal business needs into scalable technical solutions
Excel at cross-functional collaboration and can communicate effectively with both technical and legal stakeholders
Self-directed and can manage multiple technical projects simultaneously
Preferred qualifications
At least 5 years of relevant experience in legal operations, legal technology, or technical roles supporting legal teams
Technical aptitude with system integration knowledge
Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science
Excellent verbal and written communication, analytical, collaboration, and interpersonal skills
Proven project management skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, manage multiple projects simultaneously, and deliver quality results
Collaborative team player mindset with genuine interest in technology development and AI, thriving in fast-paced environments
Role-specific policy:
For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or New York office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time.
The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
Annual Salary:
$170,000
—

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

jobs.description: Do you want to shape how every Amazonian meets, collaborates, and gets work done in an AI-native world? Enterprise Foundational AI (EFAI) is building the foundational AI products and primitives that power Amazonian productivity globally, and we are looking for a Manager III, Software Development to lead our Meetings, Collaboration & Productivity team. You will lead a team of 10+ engineers building both the reusable AI building blocks that Amazon builders compose and the end-to-end products that any Amazonian can adopt, while driving a Tier 1 service to a clean, well-managed completion. Own high-impact scope: collaboration intelligence, and pre-/in-/post-meeting workflows used across Amazon. Build for leverage: deliver primitives that other builders reuse and core products that solve common workflows independent of org or role. Lead at the frontier: make AI an embedded, intuitive layer in how Amazonians work, not a separate tool to adopt. Grow people: develop engineers across levels and shape the next generation of technical and people leaders. Key job responsibilities - Lead, coach, and grow a team of 10+ software engineers, owning performance, career development, in-flight promotions, and hiring. - Own delivery, operational excellence, and on-call health for Tier 1 service through its lifecycle, from launch to deprecation. - Set and communicate clear priorities, maintaining top priority services at large scale while phasing in new initiatives on a capacity-driven timeline. - Deliver primitives (for example the Meeting Agent Platform, and meeting data APIs) that other Amazon builders compose into their own products. - Deliver core, end-to-end products (collaboration intelligence, pre-/in-/post-meeting workflows) that Amazonians adopt regardless of role. - Partner across organizations to sequence migrations and launches safely, and communicate timelines, capacity, and risk transparently to stakeholders. - Instrument outcomes so enterprises have clear line-of-sight into how their productivity grows. A day in the life Your day spans two worlds. In the morning you might review the phased rollout of a service authentication workflow and aligning with partner and security teams on rollback safeguards before accelerating traffic. Mid-day you meet with product and stakeholders on the Agent Platform roadmap, unblocking builders who compose your primitives into their own agents. In the afternoon you hold 1:1s with engineers and review a design for a post-meeting workflow. Throughout, you keep the team anchored on meetings and collaborations as the top priority while giving them a clear, motivating line of sight into the forward roadmap. About the team Enterprise Foundational AI (EFAI) accelerates Amazon's AI-native transformation by building, integrating, and scaling foundational AI products and experiences that power Amazonian productivity globally. We deliver two categories of work: technical primitives, the unified, secure, and intelligent building blocks that AI application builders compose to ship faster without reinventing common capabilities; and core AI products and experiences that solve end-to-end use cases common across Amazon, independent of organization or job role. The Meetings, Collaboration & Productivity team is EFAI's engine for how Amazonians meet, collaborate, and get work done. We build both layers of that model within our domain: primitives such as the Agent Platform, calendar MCP tools, and scheduling building blocks; and core products such as post-meeting agentic workflows. Our culture pairs high operational standards with genuine invention: we hold a Tier 1 service bar while inventing the AI-native experiences that will replace the old ways of working. Our aspiration, shared across EFAI, is that within a year every Amazonian uses AI as an embedded, intuitive part of how work gets done, so people focus on high-judgment decisions, creativity, and customer obsession while AI handles high-volume, repeatable work end-to-end.

Des projets créatifs et engagés;

The Director will also provide strategic oversight of broader domestic and regional demand, ensuring clear visibility into current priorities, capacity, work in flight, and the backlog. Working with product and technology leaders, the Director will help shape prioritization decisions and ensure regional teams receive timely, transparent guidance on whether requests can be accommodated and when. This is a hands-on role that connects strategy to execution. The Director will partner with product delivery, release management, VisaNet, OVN, and regional teams to improve intake and handoffs, reduce the time required to reach decisions, expand adoption of the agentic toolchain, and identify opportunities for greater reuse and standardization. Key Responsibilities Localization and Sovereignty Platform Strategy Own and evolve Visa's strategy for domestic processing, localization, and sovereignty across the platform portfolio. Partner with regional, market, and corporate strategy teams to define new platform offerings, deployment models, and operating approaches that address evolving market and sovereignty requirements. Develop recommendations for how market needs should be addressed across global VisaNet capabilities, localized deployments, OVN-based solutions, and sovereign platform models. Identify opportunities for reusable capabilities and common platform patterns that reduce reliance on market-specific solutions and accelerate future deployments. VisaNet and OVN Roadmap and Solutioning Own the strategic relationship between VisaNet and OVN for domestic and regional processing initiatives. Regional Demand Management and Communication Maintain a consolidated view of regional demand, work in flight, backlog, and investment priorities. Lead monthly regional reviews and communicate roadmap priorities, delivery expectations, and tradeoffs. Identify opportunities for platform reuse and common solutions across markets while highlighting areas that require unique local treatment. Partner with product and technology leaders on prioritization decisions and capacity tradeoffs. Ensure stakeholders receive timely and transparent guidance regarding request disposition and expected delivery timing. Improve intake quality, handoffs, and decision-making processes. Ensure domestic, regional, and sovereign market needs are understood, represented, and reflected in platform strategy, roadmap discussions, and modernization planning.. Cross-Functional Partnership and Communication Build trusted relationships across product, technology, strategy, risk, compliance, release management, delivery, and regional teams. Bring together VisaNet, OVN, regional, product, and technology stakeholders to resolve cross-platform dependencies, communicate decisions, and drive alignment on strategic priorities. Develop executive-ready views of regional demand, roadmap priorities, capacity constraints, and investment tradeoffs, providing leadership with clear visibility into domestic processing, localization, and sovereignty initiatives across markets. Promote adoption of agentic ways of working that improve visibility, coordination, and decision speed. New market requirements are increasingly addressed through reusable capabilities, common platform patterns, and repeatable deployment approaches rather than one-off solutions. Leadership has clear visibility into regional demand, strategic priorities, key tradeoffs, and the status of domestic processing, localization, and sovereignty initiatives across markets. Regional, VisaNet, and OVN teams collaborate effectively, with improved intake quality, reduced handoff friction, faster prioritization decisions, and greater transparency into dependencies and platform direction. Strong analytical skills; able to look at a set of client, market, and technology inputs and turn them into a clear recommendation on what to prioritize. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As a Deployment Manager on the Beneficial Deployments team, you will guide customers from a signed contract into a live, governed, and adopted deployment so that customers achieve tangible impact rather than simply incremental improvement with Claude. You'll guide organizations from contract signature to production deployment across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and our API products, fundamentally changing how they work and deliver on their missions.
You'll be the technical hands that switch Claude on. Before any organization can drive adoption, before any champion can ship their first workflow, someone has to connect Claude to the customer's identity provider, get the right people provisioned into the right workspaces, and walk their CISO through how it all comes together. That's your work. You turn "we've signed the contract" into "our employees can log in, with the right access, under the right policies, the way our security team expects."
This is a high-leverage role where you'll pioneer scalable activation methodologies that enable hundreds of nonprofit customers to unlock transformative use cases and realize measurable outcomes at unprecedented speed. You won't just follow playbooks. You'll design the frameworks and repeatable processes that can be deployed consistently across diverse customer environments, and you'll shape them into programs that reach customers we could never serve one at a time.
You'll operate at the intersection of technical deployment, enablement, and program design. Some days you'll be in the weeds with a customer's IT team debugging a SAML assertion; other days you'll be stepping back to ask how the last ten deployments should change the next hundred. Your systems-thinking approach will directly shape how we activate customers, and your strategic management will ensure every customer achieves meaningful outcomes within their first 90 days. By identifying patterns across activations, you'll build replicable approaches to organizational change while maintaining the agility to customize solutions for each customer's unique transformation journey.
Responsibilities:
Own the complete activation journey from contract signature to production deployment, orchestrating cross-functional resources and customer teams to ensure rapid time-to-value across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and API products.
Deploy Claude inside customer environments. Configure and troubleshoot SSO (SAML), SCIM and JIT provisioning, MCP connectors, admin policy templates, and seat-assignment logic across Okta, Entra ID, Ping, and Google Workspace. Deliver informative transitions to Support for deeper issues that require investigation or engineering support.
Act as a trusted advisor to customer CISOs and CTOs on governance and enterprise setup. Bring a clear point of view on best practices, help security and IT leadership make the design decisions that determine whether a deployment holds up over time
Light up the capabilities that make Claude valuable. Enable and govern MCP connectors to the customer's systems, ensure Skills, Projects, and other capabilities are turned on and configured for their use cases, and work with their IT team on the approvals and OAuth consent this requires, so that day one feels ready
Design and scale activation frameworks by identifying patterns across deployments and building templated playbooks that balance standardization with customization for breakthrough outcomes.
Turn playbooks into programs. Package what works into repeatable, increasingly self-serve motions (deployment checklists, admin enablement sessions, onboarding cohorts, Claude-powered guidance) so that activation quality no longer depends on you being in the room.
Drive organizational transformation by developing change management strategies, rollout plans, and Train-the-Trainer programs that build internal AI champions and catalyze adoption across customer organizations.
Define and track success metrics across activation rate, time-to-value, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency, using data to continuously optimize the motion.
Channel customer insights back to Product, Support, and Security teams, serving as voice of the customer so that repeat deployment blockers get solved once.
You may be a good fit if you have:
5+ years in customer-facing technical roles such as implementation management, technical account management, technical onboarding, solutions consulting, or customer success, with a track record of running multiple concurrent enterprise deployments with documented handoffs.
Experience serving nonprofits or mission-driven organizations. You've worked with (or inside) them and you understand how they differ from commercial enterprises.
Hands-on, sustained ownership of enterprise identity integration work. SAML, OIDC, SCIM v2, and JIT provisioning across at least two major identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, Ping, Google Workspace). You can debug a broken SAML assertion or a misconfigured SCIM attribute map without escalating, and you know when a Support handoff is the right call.
Experience advising CISOs, CTOs, or IT leadership on enterprise governance and setup for a SaaS or AI platform, with an informed point of view on org topology, access models, RBAC, and OAuth.
Working knowledge of security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) sufficient to anticipate what a customer's security review will ask, and to know when to bring in our AI Security Specialist.
You've designed, shipped, and measured programs that serve many customers at once: onboarding cohorts, enablement series, admin academies, lifecycle or engagement motions. You naturally ask "how might we scale this?", turn 1:1 moments into 1:many programs, and instrument what you build so you know what's working.
Hands-on fluency with AI in your own workflow. You've prototyped, generated content, analyzed accounts, or replaced internal processes with LLMs, and you can talk concretely about what worked, what didn't, and what's next. You don't wait for AI tooling to arrive; you build it.
Organizational change and enablement experience including developing rollout strategies, navigating stakeholder resistance, building internal champions, and designing programs that drive adoption at scale.
Comfort building in ambiguity. This is a new role on the team, and what you build becomes the template. You'll thrive creating structure where none exists, adapting quickly as the business evolves, and learning continuously.
Data-driven and metrics-oriented. Experience setting and tracking success metrics from day one, using data to optimize approaches, and demonstrating impact to diverse stakeholders.
